annotations.title: Relationships between companies, investors and people

description: Returns the relationship graph around a company, an investment house or a person — every relationship a filed fact with the filings that prove it: who holds the company (13F, Schedule 13D/G, Form 4: share of capital), which companies hold shares of other companies (invests_in: NVIDIA in CoreWeave, Alphabet in SpaceX), its officers and directors and their roles, who holds warrants, convertibles or preferred shares in it (holds_rights_in: AMD's warrant to Meta, Akamai's to Anthropic), and who buys from whom: the customers a company names in its own filings, with their share of its revenue (customer_of, from the customer to the company that names it: NVIDIA is 16% of Fabrinet's revenue, Apple 91% of Cirrus Logic's, Samsung a customer of Applied Materials, Qorvo and FormFactor) — and the contracts named in 8-K, 6-K, 10-Q, 10-K and prospectuses: customer_of when the filing says who buys from whom (Microsoft and NVIDIA from IREN, OpenAI from CoreWeave, Anthropic and Fluidstack leasing from TeraWulf), agreement_with when it does not (Intel and NVIDIA), each contract with its title, value as stated, term, megawatts, signing date and document — and who acquired whom: acquired, from the buyer to what it acquired, whichever side filed it (Skyworks and Qorvo; AMD and ZT Systems; Sanmina buying ZT Systems' manufacturing business from AMD), each deal with what changed hands (the company, a business, a stake), agreed or completed, its date, the full price when stated and its document — and who lends to whom: lends_to, from a lender or the agent of a facility to the company whose filing names it (MUFG, Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan as agents of CoreWeave's term loans), each facility with its kind, status, amount and filing, and its life as filed — the date of its agreement, its margin, its maturity and extension option, its end or extension (a lender whose facilities have all ended or matured is expired); and the named buyers of a company's shares (invests_in with instruments: NVIDIA buying 214,776,632 Intel shares) — then, as sources are added, suppliers named in annual reports and competitors named by the company. Private companies are nodes too (Anthropic, OpenAI, Nscale): named by a filing, with no price or financials; one that has filed a surveyed prospectus also has the links it states (Anthropic: its suppliers and what it committed to pay each, Amazon's and Google's stakes rebuilt as floors, the agent of its credit facility, the counterparties of its note purchase facilities, AMD's commitment to buy its shares). `depth: 2` adds the neighbours' relationships (who else Vanguard holds, where else a director sits). Use it when the user asks how companies are connected, who is behind a company, or what links two of them. For the full list of a company's shareholders with bounds and moves, use get_ownership; for one investor's portfolio, get_holders.

center.description: The company, house or person at the center: a ticker, a company name (listed or not: 'Anthropic'), a holder's key or name ('vanguard', 'Elon Musk'), or a typed id from a previous answer (company:nvda, holder:vanguard, person:<id>, gov:us).

depth.description: 1 (default): the center's relationships; 2: its neighbours' too.

limit.description: How many relationships at most (default 40, max 200).

minShare.description: Minimum share of capital, as a fraction (0.01 = 1%), for ownership relationships.

natures.description: Comma-separated natures within the view: owns, invests_in, holds_rights_in, insider_of, customer_of, supplier_of, agreement_with, acquired, competes_with, lends_to.

since.description: Only relationships whose proving filing is dated on or after this day (YYYY-MM-DD).

status.description: 'active' (default): relationships the filings still state — a customer the supplier's latest report still names, a contract not past its stated term; 'all': past ones too, each with its relationshipStatus (not_restated, expired).

name: get_relationships
title: Relationships between companies, investors and people
